mainTopic: Who may testify that a בכור's blemish was not made on purpose: shepherds, outside witnesses, ישראל owners and a כהן's household, with the views of רבי מאיר and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
overview: This amud deals with who is believed to testify that a בכור's blemish happened naturally and was not made on purpose. It first finishes one reading of the משנה: a כהן shepherding for a ישראל is believed, but a ישראל shepherding for a כהן is not, and a כהן testifying for another כהן certainly is not. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל trusts a כהן about another's בכור, while רבי מאיר says one suspected on a matter may never judge or testify about it. The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר is needed under the other reading, and answers with the ברייתא of רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי, who requires two outside witnesses. רב קטינא follows that view for a ספק בכור in a ישראל's house. רב נחמן disagrees and proves that the ישראל owner himself is believed, because only כהנים are suspected of causing blemishes. The final הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: a כהן's son or daughter may testify, but not his wife, since אשתו כגופו. The amud ends with רב פפא asking אביי how, according to רבי מאיר, כהנים could ever serve as judges. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Why a priest-shepherd working for an Israelite is believed
steps.stepSummary: A כהן who shepherds for a ישראל has no reason to lie, because he assumes the owner will give the בכור to a learned כהן and not to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He says to himself: the owner will not pass over a Torah scholar and give it to me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why 'רועי ישראל', meaning כהנים who work for a ישראל owner, are believed. The owner chooses which כהן gets the בכור, and the shepherd assumes it will not be him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We only distrust a witness who might gain from his testimony. Here the shepherd-כהן expects the owner to give the בכור to a תלמיד חכם כהן, so he gains nothing by lying. That is why his testimony is accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say (to himself); describes the witness's thinking
Leaves aside, passes over
A young Torah scholar
To me

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רועי ישראל' does not mean the shepherds are ישראלים. It means shepherds of a ישראל owner, and the shepherds themselves are כהנים.

phrases.english: He says (to himself):
He (the owner) will not pass over a Torah scholar
phrases.notes: The owner will prefer a learned כהן

phrases.english: and give it to me.
phrases.notes: So the shepherd gains nothing by lying

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵימָר אָמַר: לָא שָׁבֵיק צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reasoning of the second reading of the משנה, which began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן shepherding for a ישראל is believed, because he has no expected gain.

steps.title: Israelite shepherds of a priest are not believed
steps.stepSummary: 'רועי כהנים' means ישראלים shepherding for a כהן. They are not believed because they may lie in exchange for a taste of the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Priest-shepherds' are cases where the shepherds are Israelites. They are not believed, because we worry about a mouthful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the משנה's second case, 'רועי כהנים'. These are ישראל shepherds working for a כהן owner, and they are not believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the owner is a כהן who owns the בכור and may eat it himself once it is declared blemished. A ישראל shepherd might lie to help him and hope to be given a bite of the meat. This possible gain disqualifies his testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: Shepherds of כהנים (here, ישראלים working for a כהן)
Believed, trustworthy as witnesses
We are concerned
A swallow or mouthful (a small reward of food)

phrases.english: 'Priest-shepherds' means the shepherds are Israelites —
they are not believed,
because we are concerned about a mouthful.
phrases.notes: He might lie to get a taste of the meat

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the believed case to the case that is not believed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ישראל shepherding for a כהן is not believed, because of the concern of לגימא.

steps.title: A priest testifying for another priest is surely not believed
steps.stepSummary: A כהן testifying about another כהן's בכור carries two concerns: a returned favor and a mouthful.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the more so a priest for a priest: we worry about returning favors, and we worry about a mouthful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a stronger case. A כהן shepherd testifying for a כהן owner is certainly not believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ישראל shepherd raises only one concern, the mouthful. A כהן raises a second one as well: he may help his fellow כהן now so that the favor is returned on his own בכור later. With two concerns, this case follows by קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so (a stronger case)
Repaying favors, reciprocal 'you help me, I help you'

phrases.english: And all the more so a priest for a priest,
because we are concerned about returned favors,
phrases.notes: He helps now and gets help on his own בכור later

phrases.english: and we are concerned about a mouthful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a stronger case on the previous one by קל וחומר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן testifying for another כהן is not believed, because of both גומלין and לגימא.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: believed for another, not for himself
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that a כהן is believed about another כהן's בכור, but not about his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבן שמעון comes to say: he is believed about his friend's animal, but not believed about his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds in the משנה. He believes a כהן testifying for a fellow כהן, and disbelieves him only about his own animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not accept the worry of גומלין, the returned favor. He disqualifies only direct self-interest, meaning testimony about one's own בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, a תנא in the משנה
And he comes to say (his added opinion)
His fellow (another כהן)
Himself

phrases.english: And רבן שמעון comes to say:
he is believed about his fellow's animal,
but is not believed about his own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the view of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who disagrees with the כהן-for-כהן ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן is believed about another's בכור, but not about his own.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: a suspect person may not judge or testify
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that a person suspected about a matter may not judge it or testify about it, even with no personal gain.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר comes to say: one who is suspect on a matter may not judge it and may not testify about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי מאיר's view in this reading. Even a כהן working for a ישראל, who gains nothing, is disqualified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא believed כהנים shepherding for a ישראל because they have no gain. רבי מאיר disagrees. Since כהנים as a group are suspected of blemishing בכורות, they may not testify on this matter at all, even when no gain is involved.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is suspected regarding this matter
He may not judge it
And he may not testify about it

steps.whatToRemember: In this reading, the תנא קמא believes כהנים working for a ישראל, and רבי מאיר disagrees, holding that a suspect person may never testify on the matter.

phrases.english: And רבי מאיר comes to say:
one who is suspect on the matter,
may neither judge it nor testify about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes this reading of the משנה with רבי מאיר's view, which disagrees with step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone suspected on a matter may not judge or testify about it, even with no gain.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's view fits the second reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא grants that according to the reading where כהנים working for a ישראל are believed, רבי מאיר is adding something new.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is fine according to the one who says Israelite-shepherds are priests and are believed. That is why רבי מאיר comes to say: one suspect on a matter may neither judge nor testify.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. Using 'בשלמא', the גמרא first shows which reading has no problem, and it is preparing to challenge the other reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תנא קמא believes כהנים who work for a ישראל, then רבי מאיר clearly disagrees with him and has a reason to speak. This sets the standard for the question about to follow.

keyTerms.meaning: It is fine (according to one view); sets up a contrast
According to the one who says
That is why

phrases.english: It is fine according to the one who says:
'Israelite shepherds' are priests, and they are believed —
that is why רבי מאיר comes to say:
one suspect on the matter
may neither judge it nor testify about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from explaining the משנה to testing the two readings against רבי מאיר's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: Sets up a challenge to the first reading of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Shows that under the second reading רבי מאיר says something new, which sets the standard for the next step.

steps.title: Under the first reading, רבי מאיר seems redundant
steps.stepSummary: According to the reading where כהנים working for a ישראל are not believed, רבי מאיר seems to say exactly what the תנא קמא said.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says priest-shepherds in an Israelite's house are not believed, what is רבי מאיר teaching us? That is the same as the תנא קמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks its question. In the first reading, רבי מאיר seems to add nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first reading, the תנא קמא already disqualifies כהנים working for a ישראל. רבי מאיר's rule that a suspect person may not testify gives the same result. A תנא should not repeat what has already been said, so the first reading needs a defense.

keyTerms.meaning: But (introduces the side with a problem)
In the house (employ) of a ישראל
What does he come to teach us?
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not that רבי מאיר is wrong. The question is that, under the first reading, his statement seems to add nothing new.

phrases.english: But according to the one who says:

phrases.aramaic: רוֹעֵי כֹהֲנִים בֵּי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵין נֶאֱמָנִין —
phrases.english: priest-shepherds in an Israelite's house are not believed —
what does רבי מאיר come to teach us?
That is the same as the first תנא!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'בשלמא... אלא' structure by challenging the first reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first reading of the משנה, in which the תנא קמא disqualifies כהנים working for a ישראל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the תנא קמא already disqualifies them, רבי מאיר's rule adds nothing, so the two opinions would be identical.

steps.title: The difference between them is the view of רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא and רבי מאיר differ over the view of רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי, who requires two outside witnesses for a כהן's בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them regarding the view of רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי. A ברייתא teaches that רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי says: a בכור in a כהן's house needs two people 'from the marketplace' to testify about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 7. It shows that the תנא קמא and רבי מאיר really do disagree, and their disagreement is about the view of רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי only asks that the witnesses come 'from the marketplace', meaning people outside the כהן's household. He does not say they cannot be כהנים. So the תנא קמא agrees with him that an outside כהן who is not the shepherd is believed, while רבי מאיר does not trust any כהן, even an outside one.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them (a practical point where two views give different results)
As it is taught (in a ברייתא)
A firstborn animal in the possession of a כהן
Two people 'from the marketplace', meaning outsiders who are not from the owner's household

steps.confusionAlert: 'From the marketplace' does not mean 'non-כהנים'. It only means people who are not part of the owner's household. That is exactly why an outside כהן can still count, and that point is what separates the תנא קמא from רבי מאיר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer saves רבי מאיר's statement from being a pointless repeat. His general rule about suspected people adds a real new point: even an independent כהן is not believed.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
regarding the view of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefusai,
phrases.notes: The תנא קמא agrees with him, and רבי מאיר does not.

phrases.english: as it is taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefusai says:
A firstborn animal in the house of a priest
phrases.notes: It developed a blemish, and we need to know the blemish was not made on purpose.

phrases.english: requires two people from the marketplace
phrases.notes: Outsiders, not household members. They could even be כהנים.

phrases.english: to testify about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קַפּוֹסַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7 that רבי מאיר appears to repeat the תנא קמא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a practical difference (נפקא מינה) between the two views
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the תנא קמא and רבי מאיר both disqualify כהנים in the same way, so רבי מאיר adds nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא accepts an independent כהן as a witness, as רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי does. רבי מאיר rejects even an independent כהן.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: a lenient view and a strict view about household members
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows even the כהן's son or daughter to testify. רבי יוסי says even ten household members cannot testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: even his son, even his daughter may testify. רבי יוסי says: even if there are ten people, if they are members of his household, they cannot testify about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the same ברייתא. It adds two more opinions about who may testify on a כהן's בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is the most lenient: he trusts even the כהן's own children. רבי יוסי is strict about the household: the number of witnesses does not help if they all belong to the owner's house. So רבי יוסי agrees with רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי that only outsiders count, and stresses that more household witnesses do not fix the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Even his son
Members of his household
They may not testify about it

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Even his son, even his daughter may testify.
phrases.notes: This is the most lenient view.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Even ten people,
if they are members of his household,
may not testify about it.
phrases.notes: A larger number does not help when they all come from his household.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ בְּנוֹ, אֲפִילּוּ בִּתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא brought in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל accepts even the כהן's children as witnesses. רבי יוסי rejects household members no matter how many there are.

steps.title: Whose view does רב קטינא follow about a doubtful בכור in a ישראל's house?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא is the source of רב קטינא's ruling that a ספק בכור born in a ישראל's house needs two outside witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this follow? רב חסדא said in the name of רב קטינא: a doubtful firstborn that was born in a ישראל's house needs two people 'from the marketplace' to testify about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related ruling of an אמורא and asks which תנא it matches. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a ספק בכור, the animal stays with the ישראל, and he may eat it once it has a blemish. So the ישראל owner gains from a blemish, just like a כהן does with his own בכור. The question is which opinion from the ברייתא demands outside witnesses in such a case.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view does it follow?
An animal that may or may not be a firstborn
In the possession of a ישראל (a non-כהן)

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is that

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַב קַטִּינָא:
phrases.english: which Rav Ḥisda said in the name of Rav Ketina:
a doubtful firstborn that was born in the house of an Israelite
phrases.notes: For example, it is unclear whether the mother had given birth before. The ישראל keeps the animal and may eat it once it is blemished.

phrases.aramaic: צָרִיךְ שְׁנַיִם מִן הַשּׁוּק לְהָעִיד עָלָיו?
phrases.english: requires two people from the marketplace to testify about it?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַב קַטִּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא just quoted to find the source of a later אמורא's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא is the basis for requiring two outside witnesses for a ספק בכור in a ישראל's possession.

steps.title: רב קטינא follows רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי
steps.stepSummary: רב קטינא's ruling matches רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי, who requires two outside witnesses whenever the owner could be suspected.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is it? It follows רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. רב קטינא's ruling comes from רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי demands two outside witnesses for a כהן's בכור because the owner may have caused the blemish on purpose. רב קטינא applies the same logic to a ישראל who keeps a ספק בכור, since he too benefits from a blemish and is therefore suspected.

keyTerms.meaning: In accordance with whom?

steps.whatToRemember: Whenever an owner gains from a blemish, whether he is a כהן with a בכור or a ישראל with a ספק בכור, רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי requires two outside witnesses who are not from his household. The תנא קמא follows this view and accepts an independent כהן, while רבי מאיר does not trust any כהן.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?
In accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefusai.
phrases.notes: An owner who benefits from a blemish needs outside witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב קטינא's ruling follows רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי, who requires two outside witnesses when the owner benefits from a blemish.

steps.title: רב נחמן: The Owners May Testify
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that the ישראל owners themselves may testify about the blemish on a ספק בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The owners may testify about it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא, רב נחמן, disagrees with רב קטינא and says the ישראל owner is believed about his animal's blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב קטינא required two outside witnesses, as רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי does. רב נחמן says no outside witnesses are needed: the owner himself can testify. The next steps give his proof.

keyTerms.meaning: The owners of the animal
They may testify about it (that the blemish happened naturally)
An אמורא who disagrees with רב קטינא here

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
The owners may testify about it,
phrases.notes: Here "it" means the ספק בכור's blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב קטינא's ruling, which was traced to רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ישראל owner is believed to testify that his own ספק בכור's blemish was not caused on purpose.

steps.title: First Proof: Who Could Testify About מעשר?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן argues that if owners were not believed, no one could ever testify about a blemished מעשר בהמה according to רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you do not say so, then for an animal tithe, according to רבי מאיר, who could testify about it?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a proof. If owners are not believed, then according to רבי מאיר no one could ever testify about a blemished tithe animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that anyone suspected in a matter cannot judge or testify about it for others either. A blemished מעשר בהמה may be eaten, just like a בכור. So if owners were suspected of causing blemishes, no one would be left to testify. That means owners must be believed.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you do not say so (a proof formula: otherwise there is a problem)
Here, מעשר בהמה: the tenth animal of the flock, which is made holy
Who would testify about it?

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
then for an animal tithe, according to Rabbi Meir,
who testifies about it?
phrases.notes: This is a rhetorical question: no one would be left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב נחמן's ruling from Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That owners are believed about blemishes.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The logic of רבי מאיר's view applied to a blemished מעשר בהמה.

steps.title: מעשר Is Different: The Owner Gains Nothing by Lying
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. With מעשר the owner is believed for a special reason: he could have legally blemished his whole flock beforehand.
steps.simpleTranslation: With מעשר he is certainly believed, because if he wanted, he could put a blemish on his entire flock.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the מעשר proof. מעשר is a special case where the owner has no reason to cheat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before tithing, the animals are not yet holy, so the owner may blemish them all if he wishes. Since he could have done that legally, he has no reason to lie later about a blemish. This tells us nothing about a בכור, which is holy from birth.

keyTerms.meaning: He is certainly believed
Throws (puts) a blemish on it
His flock

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean a person may blemish holy animals. The animals here are blemished before they become מעשר, while they are still ordinary animals.

phrases.english: With the tithe, he is certainly believed,
because if he wants, he can put a blemish
on his entire flock.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from מעשר in Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the מעשר example is rejected, not רב נחמן's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: With מעשר the owner has no motive to lie, so this case cannot show that owners are believed about a בכור.

steps.title: Rebuilt Proof: Who Could Testify About a ספק בכור?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן's proof is restated with ספק בכור: if the owner is not believed, who could testify about it according to רבי מאיר?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, for a ספק בכור, according to רבי מאיר, who could testify about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rewords רב נחמן's proof. It swaps the weak מעשר example for a ספק בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a ספק בכור, both the ישראל owner and a כהן could gain from a blemish. So the special reason from מעשר does not apply. If owners were not believed, according to רבי מאיר no one at all could testify about it.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that may or may not be a firstborn
Rather (here it introduces a corrected version of the argument)

phrases.english: Rather, an animal of uncertain firstborn status,
according to Rabbi Meir, who testifies about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rebuilds the proof after the מעשר version was rejected in Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That a ישראל owner is believed about a ספק בכור's blemish.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The logic of רבי מאיר's view: otherwise no witness would be possible.

steps.title: Suggestion: Maybe a ספק בכור Has No Solution
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a possible escape: maybe רבי מאיר really holds that a ספק בכור has no way to be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: indeed, it has no remedy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way out of the proof: maybe it is true that no one can testify, and the animal simply can never be eaten. This sets up the next step, which knocks the suggestion down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in Step 15 assumes that a ספק בכור must have some way to be eaten. This suggestion questions that assumption: maybe according to רבי מאיר it is simply stuck. If so, the proof would fail.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (it brings up a possible objection)
Indeed, that is so
A remedy, a way to fix the situation

phrases.english: And if you would say: indeed so,
that it has no remedy,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to block the proof in Step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: This suggestion targets the hidden assumption of the proof, not רב נחמן's ruling directly.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes a ספק בכור can be eaten. Maybe רבי מאיר holds it never can.

steps.title: משנה Shows רבי מאיר Lets a ספק בכור Be Eaten
steps.stepSummary: A משנה shows that רבי מאיר discusses מתנות from a slaughtered ספק בכור, so he must allow it to be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: רבי יוסי used to say that any animal whose replacement is in the hands of a כהן is exempt from the gifts, and רבי מאיר obligates.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה to knock down the suggestion in Step 16. The משנה shows that רבי מאיר does allow a ספק בכור to be slaughtered and eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר requires the meat gifts (מתנות) to be given from a slaughtered ספק בכור. That only makes sense if it may be eaten. But it may only be eaten after a blemish is confirmed, so someone must be able to testify about the blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה (introduces a source that contradicts)
Its replacement, a substitute animal
The meat gifts given to a כהן from a slaughtered animal (foreleg, cheeks, stomach)
Obligates

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the key step. The proof works because רבי מאיר's own ruling in the משנה assumes the animal can be eaten.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: Rabbi Yosei would say:
Any animal whose replacement is in the hand of a priest
is exempt from the priestly gifts,
and Rabbi Meir obligates!
phrases.notes: This means רבי מאיר is talking about a ספק בכור that was slaughtered and eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the suggestion in Step 16 and so restores the proof in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That according to רבי מאיר a ספק בכור can be eaten, so someone must be able to testify about its blemish.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (בכורות 18b) where רבי מאיר requires מתנות from such an animal.

steps.title: Conclusion: Only כהנים Are Suspected About Blemishes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that owners may testify, because only כהנים are suspected of causing blemishes, not ישראלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: the owners may testify about it. It is כהנים who are suspected about blemishes; ישראלים are not suspected about blemishes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that רב נחמן is right: a ישראל owner is believed about his ספק בכור's blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי מאיר lets a ספק בכור be eaten, someone must be able to testify, and that is the ישראל owner. The reason is that only כהנים, who normally receive firstborns and gain from blemishes, are suspected of causing them. A ישראל does not have that suspicion.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (a conclusion formula)
Suspected
About blemishes

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן: a ישראל owner may testify about his ספק בכור's blemish, because only כהנים are suspected of causing blemishes. This disagrees with רב קטינא, who required two outside witnesses.
steps.confusionAlert: The suspicion is about who usually gains from blemishing a בכור, which is the כהן. It is not a general statement about anyone's honesty.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this:
the owners may testify about it,
it is priests who are suspected about blemishes,
Israelites are not suspected about blemishes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the proof completed in Step 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A ישראל owner is believed about his ספק בכור's blemish, because only כהנים are suspected of causing blemishes.

steps.title: רב נחמן and רבא disagree about the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. רבא rules like רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב נחמן said the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. רבא said the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two אמוראים who disagree about which תנא to follow. The question is whether a כהן's household members may testify about his blemished בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל trusts the כהן's family to say the blemish was not man-made. רבי יוסי does not trust them, because they are too close to the owner. רב נחמן follows the lenient view and רבא follows the strict view.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a statement or dispute of אמוראים)
The practical law follows...
His household members

phrases.english: It was stated: Rav Nachman said:
The halacha is like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
Rava said: The halacha is like Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא from step 9 and gives the practical halacha in the dispute there between רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי יוסי about household members testifying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן: household members are believed (like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל). רבא: they are not believed (like רבי יוסי).

steps.title: רבא seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: Another statement of רבא appears to let the household testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבא really say this? But רבא said: if the owner was standing outside with us, and the animal went in whole and came out injured, they may testify about it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא with a different statement of his. In that statement he seems to allow the household to testify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבא's case, the animal went into the house healthy and came out injured, while the כהן owner stood outside. רבא says testimony is accepted there. That seems to trust the people connected to the owner, which contradicts his ruling like רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: And did he really say so? (introduces a contradiction)
The owners
Injured, blemished
They may testify about it

phrases.english: And did Rava really say this?
But didn't Rava say:
If the owner is standing outside with us,
and the animal went in whole and came out injured —
they may testify about it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רָבָא הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's ruling from Step 19.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא elsewhere accepts testimony in a case involving the owner's household, which is a contradiction.

steps.title: All the household was outside
steps.stepSummary: רבא's case is one where every family member was outside, and only the shepherd was inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: all the owners, meaning the whole household, were standing outside, and we are not suspicious of the one who testifies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading רבא's case differently. The whole family was outside, so the witness is not a family member at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the shepherd was inside with the animal. He is the one testifying, not the family. So רבא never trusted household members, and his ruling like רבי יוסי stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (reinterpret the statement as)
And we are not concerned

phrases.english: Say: all the owners were standing outside,
and we are not concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from Step 20.
steps.terutzMaskana: The household was all outside. The shepherd, who is not family, testifies.

steps.title: Then why say it at all?
steps.stepSummary: If the witness is an outsider, the ruling seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the point of saying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If only an outsider testifies, of course he is believed, so why did רבא need to teach it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a 'why was this needed' challenge. It does not disagree with the law itself. It questions whether רבא's statement teaches anything new under the new reading.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
What is there to say? (it is obvious)

phrases.english: If so, what is the point of saying it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 21.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading, רבא's statement would be obvious and pointless.

steps.title: We might have suspected the shepherd
steps.stepSummary: רבא needed to teach that the shepherd is not suspected of making the blemish himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: let us suspect the shepherd. So רבא teaches us that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the ruling is not obvious. One might have thought the shepherd himself caused the blemish, since he was alone with the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shepherd was the only one inside, so he looks like a possible suspect. רבא teaches that we do not suspect him, and his testimony is accepted. That is the new information.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said
Let us worry about suspicion
It teaches us (otherwise)

phrases.english: You might have said: let us worry about suspicion,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'why say it' challenge from Step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The shepherd, alone with the animal, should be suspected.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is not suspected, and his testimony is accepted.

steps.title: Final הלכה: son and daughter yes, wife no
steps.stepSummary: The halacha follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, but only for a son or daughter. A wife cannot testify, because she is like the כהן himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, but only for his son and daughter, not his wife. Why? His wife is considered like his own self.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling. Household members may testify, but there is a limit: a wife may not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner himself is never believed about his own בכור. A son or daughter is a separate person, so they may testify. A wife is treated as one unit with her husband, so her testimony counts like his own, which is not accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה is
And specifically, only
His wife is like his own body (his own self)

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. A כהן's son or daughter may testify about his בכור, but his wife may not, because אשתו כגופו.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with רבא's ruling. רבא held like רבי יוסי, but the final הלכה goes like רב נחמן's position, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, with the wife excluded.

phrases.english: And the halacha is like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
but specifically his son and his daughter,
but not his wife.
What is the reason?
His wife is considered like his own self.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: שאלה / תשובה (for the מאי טעמא portion)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the dispute from Step 19 with a final ruling and a limit.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A כהן's son or daughter is believed about his בכור, but his wife is not, since she is like himself.

steps.title: רב פפא asks: how can כהנים be judges according to רבי מאיר?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says someone suspected on one matter is suspected on the whole Torah. If so, suspected כהנים should be unable to judge, yet a פסוק says they decide every dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: רבי מאיר says one suspected on a matter can neither judge nor testify about it. רבי מאיר also says one suspected on one matter is suspected on the whole Torah. So should כהנים also be unable to judge? But it is written: 'And by their word shall every dispute and every נגע be decided'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא opens a new question by combining two rules of רבי מאיר. Together they seem to disqualify כהנים from judging entirely, which clashes with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כהנים are suspected of blemishing בכורות so they can eat them. Rule 1: a suspected person cannot judge that matter. Rule 2: suspicion on one matter spreads to the whole Torah. Combined, כהנים could never judge anything, yet the Torah gives them a judging role. This sets up an answer that will follow.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is suspected regarding a matter
May neither judge it nor testify about it
Suspected regarding the entire Torah
But isn't it written? (challenge from a פסוק)

steps.whyThisMatters: This tests how far רבי מאיר's suspicion rule really goes. The answer will have to limit it so the Torah's judicial role for כהנים still holds.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
According to Rabbi Meir, who says

phrases.aramaic: הֶחָשׁוּד עַל הַדָּבָר לֹא דָּנוֹ וְלֹא מְעִידוֹ,
phrases.english: one suspected about a matter may neither judge it nor testify about it,
and Rabbi Meir also says
one suspected about one matter
is suspected about the entire Torah,

phrases.aramaic: כֹּהֲנִים הָכִי נָמֵי דְּלָא דָּיְינִי דִּינָא?
phrases.english: then should priests also not judge cases?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכְתִיב ״וְעַל פִּיהֶם יִהְיֶה כׇּל רִיב וְכׇל נָגַע״!
phrases.english: But it is written: "And by their word shall every dispute and every affliction be"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new line, building on the earlier idea that כהנים are suspected of causing blemishes.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's two rules about suspected people
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Combined, the two rules disqualify all כהנים from judging, which contradicts the פסוק giving them that role.
